stem: An AI team runs daily compliance auditing over 50,000 customer service transcripts every night. The audit results must be ready by 08:00 the following morning, but individual transcripts do not require real-time processing. Currently, the team runs concurrent synchronous /v1/messages calls, frequently hitting rate limits and incurring standard token costs. Which architectural change should the architect recommend to optimize cost and throughput?

options.text: Downgrade all transcripts to Claude Haiku without evaluation to lower the token pricing tier under synchronous endpoints.
Implement exponential backoff retries on the synchronous /v1/messages endpoint while keeping the immediate processing model.
Send all 50,000 transcripts concatenated into a single synchronous Messages request with max output tokens set to maximum.
Migrate the nightly evaluation pipeline to the Message Batches API to receive a 50% token cost discount and separate throughput pools.

explanation: The Anthropic Message Batches API is designed specifically for high-volume, non-real-time asynchronous workloads (such as evals, nightly audits, and batch analysis). Requests submitted via Message Batches receive a 50% discount on input and output token pricing, process within a target turnaround time of 24 hours (most finishing in under 1 hour), and operate with separate batch throughput allocations that prevent hitting standard API rate limits.

distractorNotes.opt-a: Downgrading the model blindly risks audit accuracy and compliance quality without leveraging the 50% batch discount on the appropriate model.
distractorNotes.opt-b: Retries handle rate limit errors but do not address cost inefficiency or the fundamental mismatch between real-time calls and batch workloads.
distractorNotes.opt-c: A single request exceeds context limits, lacks granular per-transcript error recovery, and risks complete failure if one transcript fails.
